title: Data Structures
description: Linear and non-linear data structures: arrays, linked lists, stacks and expression conversion, queues and deques, trees and search trees, graphs, and sorting, searching and hashing. Built from the CSC 341 lecture notes, the graph and sorting notes and the practicals; trees, linked lists and hashing, which the past papers test but the notes do not cover, are written from general knowledge.

topics.title: Data Structure Concepts and Arrays
topics.summary: A data structure organises data so it can be used efficiently; structures are primitive or non-primitive, linear or non-linear, static or dynamic. Arrays store elements of one type in contiguous memory, so an element's address is computed from the base address.
subtopics: Static and dynamic structures; abstraction and encapsulation
Number of elements and row-major and column-major addressing
Array operations: traversing, insertion, deletion, merging, copying

topics.title: Linked Lists
topics.summary: A linked list is a chain of nodes, each holding data and a pointer to the next node, so it grows and shrinks at run time. Singly, doubly and circular lists trade memory for easier movement through the list.
subtopics: Singly, doubly and circular linked lists
Insertion, deletion, traversal, search and reversal

topics.title: Stacks and Expression Conversion
topics.summary: A stack is a last-in, first-out structure where insertion (push) and deletion (pop) happen at one end, the top. Stacks check balanced parentheses and convert and evaluate infix, prefix and postfix expressions.
subtopics: push, pop, peek, isEmpty, isFull; overflow and underflow
Applications: symbol balancing, undo, recursion, DFS, backtracking
Infix, prefix and postfix notation; precedence and associativity

topics.title: Queues and Deques
topics.summary: A queue is a first-in, first-out structure: items join at the rear (enqueue) and leave from the front (dequeue). Circular queues reuse freed space, deques allow both ends, and priority queues serve the highest priority first.
subtopics: Applications: CPU and disk scheduling, buffers, printers, BFS

topics.title: Trees and Search Trees
topics.summary: A tree is a hierarchical structure of nodes with one root; binary trees are traversed in preorder, inorder or postorder. Binary search trees, AVL trees and B-trees keep keys ordered so searching stays fast.
subtopics: Root, parent, child, sibling, leaf, level and degree
Binary search trees: search, insertion, deletion

topics.title: Graphs and Spanning Trees
topics.summary: A graph is a set of vertices joined by edges, stored as an adjacency matrix or an adjacency list. Graphs are traversed depth first with a stack or breadth first with a queue, and spanning trees connect all vertices with the fewest edges.
subtopics: Vertex, edge, path and adjacency; directed and undirected graphs
Minimum spanning trees: Kruskal and Prim

topics.title: Sorting, Searching and Hashing
topics.summary: Sorting arranges data in order (bubble, selection, insertion, quick sort), and searching finds a target by linear, binary or interpolation search. Hashing maps keys to table positions directly, resolving collisions by probing or chaining.
subtopics: Bubble, selection, insertion and quick sort
Collision resolution: linear and quadratic probing, chaining
Sequential and indexed sequential file organisation
